entry.name: chucker~
entry.digest: Segment audio and reorder it on looped playback
entry.description: chucker~ takes a specified amount of audio data, stores the data in an internal buffer, divides the buffered data into equal sections, and allows the sections to be reordered on playback.

arguments.name: buffer-size-in-ms
arguments.description: An optional integer argument can be used to set the number of milliseconds to allocate for the recorded sound. (e.g. an argument of 8000 will allocate enough memory for a stereo output of 8 seconds)Note: The actual allocation will be larger than what is specified by the argument, since theobject supports two buffers and provides for double-buffering.

messages.name: directions
messages.description: The word, followed by a 1 or 2 to indicate left or right channel and a list of integer values whose length is equal to the number of steps, sets the direction of playback for the sections. Playback direction is specified as follows:1: forward (the default)0: mute-1: reverse

messages.name: fademode
messages.description: Sets the fade method for segment smoothing. Modes include:0: Classic (same as Max 5)1: Pre-fade (fades use buffered audio, fade executes prior to segment transition)2: Post-fade (fades use buffered audio, fade executes after segment transition)

messages.name: freeze
messages.digest: Loop the current buffer segment on playback
messages.description: The messagecauses the current buffer segment to loop on playback. Sending the messageresumes normal playback.

messages.name: nstep
messages.digest: Set the number of buffer segments
messages.description: The word, followed by an integer in the range 1 - 64, sets the number of equal portions into which theobject's internal buffer is segmented for playback.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: In left inlet: Left channel audio input.In middle inlet: Right channel audio input.In right inlet: An audio signal in the range 0. - 1.0 provides the audio sync input. This task is typically done using aobject's output as input.

messages.name: smooth
messages.digest: Set a crossfade amount between segments
messages.description: The word, followed by a floating point number in the range 0. - 1.0, sets an amount of smoothing (crossfading) between the individual segments being reordered for playback.

messages.name: steps
messages.digest: Set the playback order for the sections
messages.description: The word, followed by a 1 or 2 to indicate left or right channel and a list of integer values whose range is between 1 and the number of steps and whose length is equal to the number of steps, sets the order of playback for the sections.e.g. the message, when sent to aobject whose number of steps is set to 4, will play the four left channel segments in reverse order, and the right channel in regular order. order

inlets.description: The right inlet of the object accepts a signal input in the range 0. - 1.0 (typically from the right outlet of aobject) to control the playback of the object's buffered contents.

outlets.digest: Out left outlet: The segmented and reordered playback of the left channel of theobject's buffered contents.

outlets.description: Out middle outlet: The segmented and reordered playback of the right channel of theobject's buffered contents.
Out right outlet: The current step number in the playback cycle is sent out the right outlet as a signal value.Note: This is the, not the index of the segment being played back.
